title_en: Why Producers Fell From 35% of the S&P to 5% — And What It Means for Portfolios | Doug Dal
title_zh: 生产商为何从占标普 35% 跌到 5%——这对投资组合意味着什么 | Doug Daly，Core Commodity
subtitle_zh: Core Commodity 的 Doug Daly 谈上游大宗商品股票、CCNR ETF 与供给缺口下的配置价值。
summary_zh: 本期 Behind the Ticker，主持 Brad Roth 对话 Core Commodity Management 董事总经理兼投资组合经理 Doug Daly（Johns Hopkins 物理与应用数学背景，任 PM 已十三年）。核心议题是上游大宗商品生产公司（upstream producers）的配置价值：Daly 指出，这类『制造真实东西』的生产商曾占 S&P 约 35%，如今只剩约 5%，而科技股已占指数三分之一。Core Commodity 成立于 2003 年，CIO 是 Bloomberg Commodity Index（前身 Dow Jones AIG）的创造者之一，2010 年前后把自然资源股票与商品期货整合进策略（旗舰共同基金 JCRIX 约三分之一股票、三分之二期货），本策略自 2012 年独立运作，2024 年才以主动管理的 CCNR ETF（Alps Core Commodity Natural Resources ETF）形式推出。节目详解其自下而上构建：在板块层面用期货期限结构（term structure）指导超配与低配，纳入铀、农业、木材等别处罕见的敞口；并以 Freeport-McMoRan 的 Grasberg 铜矿泥石流为例（当日铜价涨 4%、股价却跌约 20%），说明持有一篮子约 12 家铜矿而非单一个股的意义。Daly 强调大宗商品与美元的负相关、不对冲外币敞口以增强『类商品』属性，以及自然资源对通胀的高敏感性（贝塔可达五到六）。战略理由是分散化与通胀保护，战术则押注基础设施、AI、近岸外包（nearshoring）与再武装（rearmament）顺风下、资本开支尚未加码带来的有利风险回报。
description: Why Producers Fell From 35% of the S&P to 5% — And What It Means for Portfolios | Doug Dal

turns.en: Welcome to Behind the Ticker, the podcast where we go beyond the symbol and into the strategy. I'm Brad Roth, founder and chief investment officer at Thor Funds, and in each episode, I sit down with ETF managers, CIOs, and industry leaders to break down how these funds are actually built, how they behave in real markets, and how advisors use them in real portfolios.
turns.zh: 欢迎收听 Behind the Ticker，在这档播客里，我们会越过股票代码（ticker），深入探究背后的策略。我是 Brad Roth，Thor Funds 的创始人兼首席投资官（chief investment officer）。每一期节目，我都会坐下来和 ETF 管理人、CIO 以及行业领袖聊一聊，拆解这些基金到底是怎么构建的、在真实市场里表现如何，以及投顾如何在真实的投资组合中使用它们。

turns.en: Most people just see a ticker symbol, but we know much more goes on behind the ticker. Hey Doug, welcome to the show. Hi Brad, thank you for having me.
turns.zh: 大多数人只看到一个代码，但我们知道，代码背后还有太多东西。嘿 Doug，欢迎来到节目。Brad 你好，谢谢你邀请我。

turns.en: So why don't you give everybody a bit about your background. I read you went to Johns Hopkins for physics and applied mathematics, and now you're managing director and portfolio manager at Core Commodity.
turns.zh: 那不如先跟大家讲讲你的背景。我了解到你在 Johns Hopkins 读的物理和应用数学，现在是 Core Commodity 的董事总经理兼投资组合经理（portfolio manager）。

turns.en: Can you kind of just walk us through your path and how you got to where you are today? Absolutely. So in college, yes, I was studying physics.
turns.zh: 能不能带我们走一遍你的经历，你是怎么走到今天这一步的？当然。大学时，是的，我学的是物理。

turns.en: I always had a pension for math. I'd been programming for a long time, and I knew I wanted a career that I could use sort of the problem-solving skills, some of the programming skills.
turns.zh: 我一直很偏爱数学。我编程已经很长时间了，我知道自己想要一份能用到这些解决问题能力、以及一部分编程技能的职业。

turns.en: And when I first learned about sort of quantitative finance and systematic trading and those sorts of things, it was really appealing to me.
turns.zh: 而当我第一次了解到量化金融（quantitative finance）、系统化交易（systematic trading）这些东西时，就觉得特别吸引我。

turns.en: And so I tacked on that applied math degree while I was there at Hopkins, and was hired shortly after graduating here at Core Commodity, where I started as an analyst.
turns.zh: 所以我在 Hopkins 读书时又加修了一个应用数学学位，毕业后不久就被 Core Commodity 招了进去，从分析师做起。

turns.en: I'm now my 13th year here as a portfolio manager, and just sort of worked my way up. It's a great organization, and it took a chance on me, and it's worked out very well.
turns.zh: 到现在我做投资组合经理已经是第 13 个年头了，一路慢慢做起来。这是个很棒的机构，它给了我机会，结果也非常好。

turns.en: Yeah, I want to talk about the firm in a little bit, but before we get there, I always like to ask people, when you're not behind the desk and work, and what do you like to do, any hobbies?
turns.zh: 嗯，我待会儿想聊聊这家公司，但在那之前，我总爱问大家一个问题：当你不在办公桌前、不工作的时候，你喜欢做点什么？有什么爱好吗？

turns.en: Yes, let's see. So I don't have a ton of free time these days. I have a two-year-old boy at home that keeps me quite busy, but I try to get up a little extra early in the morning and work out for about an hour, get some exercise in, and then at the end of the day, try to wind down with a good fiction book, non-related to work kind of reading to end the day.
turns.zh: 有，我想想。现在我空闲时间不多，家里有个两岁的男孩，让我挺忙的。但我会尽量早上早起一点，锻炼大概一个小时，做点运动；然后到一天结束时，尽量靠一本好看的虚构类小说放松下来，读点跟工作无关的东西来结束一天。

turns.en: So that's what little free time I have. That's how I've been spending it these days. Yeah, it seems to be the recurring theme of people with small kids don't have free time.
turns.zh: 所以就这点空闲时间，这就是我最近打发它的方式。是啊，这似乎是个反复出现的主题——有小孩的人都没有空闲时间。

turns.en: No, no. And I've got another on the way, so I will have even less. Well, congratulations. That's good to hear, and enjoy it while they're little, because mine are starting to grow up pretty fast.
turns.zh: 不不，我还有一个快出生了，所以以后空闲时间会更少。哦，恭喜恭喜，这是个好消息，趁孩子还小的时候好好享受吧，因为我的孩子已经开始飞快长大了。

turns.en: But let's talk about Core Commodity Management. Can you give us a quick high level on the firm, and then you guys have partnered on the product that we're going to talk about CCNR with SS and C-ALP.
turns.zh: 那我们来聊聊 Core Commodity Management 吧。能不能先给我们一个公司层面的大致介绍？另外，你们在我们今天要谈的这只产品 CCNR 上，是和 SS&C ALPS 合作的。

turns.en: So can you talk about that partnership as well? Absolutely, absolutely. So Core Commodity, as the name implies, is an asset management firm focused and dedicated on Commodity's asset management, whether that is Commodity Futures or Natural Resource Equities.
turns.zh: 那这个合作你也谈谈好吗？当然，当然。Core Commodity，顾名思义，是一家专注于、致力于大宗商品资产管理的资产管理公司，无论是商品期货（Commodity Futures）还是自然资源股票（Natural Resource Equities）。

turns.en: All we do is Commodities. It's what we live and breathe. And we were founded by some of the most senior, longstanding Commodities Futures innovators out there, dating back to many of whom date back to sort of the inception of Commodities as an asset class.
turns.zh: 我们只做大宗商品，这是我们安身立命、日夜呼吸的全部。我们的创始团队是业内一些最资深、最有资历的大宗商品期货创新者，其中很多人可以追溯到大宗商品作为一个资产类别诞生之初。

turns.en: Our CIO was the creator, one of the creators of the Bloomberg Commodity Index. Back then it was the Dow Jones AIG Commodity Index. We've also reconstituted the CRB Index.
turns.zh: 我们的 CIO 是 Bloomberg Commodity Index 的创造者之一，当时它还叫 Dow Jones AIG Commodity Index。我们还重构过 CRB Index。

turns.en: So really Commodities Indexing was our core back when we first were getting started. And then we introduced Natural Resource Equities into our strategies back in 2010 or so.
turns.zh: 所以，大宗商品指数化（Commodities Indexing）真的是我们起步时的核心。后来大约在 2010 年，我们把自然资源股票引入了我们的策略。

turns.en: The firm goes back to 2003. And we really began integrating those Natural Resource Equities along with Commodity Futures in some of our strategies back in 2010, including our flagship mutual fund product, J-C-R-I-X, which is the Complete Commodity Strategy Fund, which is where we first partnered with SS&C Alps.
turns.zh: 公司可以追溯到 2003 年。我们真正开始把自然资源股票和商品期货整合进一些策略，是在 2010 年前后，其中包括我们的旗舰共同基金产品 J-C-R-I-X，也就是 Complete Commodity Strategy Fund，那也是我们第一次和 SS&C ALPS 合作。

turns.en: So they serve as the advisor on that fund. We are the sub-advisor. And that fund has been around again since 2010 and combines Natural Resource Equities with Commodity Futures.
turns.zh: 所以在那只基金上，他们担任顾问（advisor），我们是次级顾问（sub-advisor）。那只基金同样从 2010 年就有了，把自然资源股票和商品期货结合在一起。

turns.en: It's roughly a third equities, two-thirds futures. I'm also a portfolio manager on that fund as well. And then back in 2012, we kind of launched our flagship Natural Resource Equity product, which is what is in the CCNR ETF today.
turns.zh: 大致是三分之一股票、三分之二期货。我也是那只基金的投资组合经理之一。然后在 2012 年，我们推出了旗舰的自然资源股票产品，也就是今天 CCNR ETF 里装的东西。

turns.en: So even though the ETF was launched in 2024, it's a strategy we've been running since 2012 on a standalone basis and something we think is really different because, again, the firm comes at commodities from that lens, like from that deep specialization in commodities.
turns.zh: 所以尽管这只 ETF 是 2024 年才推出的，但这个策略我们从 2012 年就在独立运作了，而且我们认为它真的很不一样，因为公司就是从那个视角、从对大宗商品的深度专精切入的。

turns.en: So as we talk more about CCNR, I think we'll get into how it really is under the hood very different from some of the other things out there.
turns.zh: 所以随着我们更多地聊 CCNR，我想我们会讲到，从内部机制（under the hood）看，它跟市面上其他一些产品到底有多不同。

turns.en: Well, that's exactly where we're going. So let's get into CCNR. It's the Alps Core Commodity Natural Resources ETF. As you said, it launched in 2024.
turns.zh: 嗯，这正是我们要谈的方向。那我们来聊聊 CCNR 吧，它是 Alps Core Commodity Natural Resources ETF。正如你所说，它在 2024 年推出。

turns.en: It's actively managed. So at a high level before we go deeper, what is this fund and what's the problem that it's solving? Absolutely. So what it is is trying to provide investors with exposure to upstream commodity producing companies to better deliver the underlying natural resources or commodity price exposure of the things those companies produce.
turns.zh: 它是主动管理型（actively managed）的。所以在深入之前，先从大方向讲，这只基金是什么？它解决的是什么问题？当然。它要做的，是给投资者提供对上游大宗商品生产公司（upstream commodity producing companies）的敞口，以更好地传递这些公司所生产的底层自然资源或商品价格敞口。

turns.en: So and why would you want to own that? Generally what we see these products use for is diversification. Fund protection is obviously the biggest thing in commodities and certainly relevant these days, but also access to growth and growth opportunities as well.
turns.zh: 那为什么要持有它呢？通常我们看到这类产品的用途是分散化（diversification）。通胀保护（inflation protection）显然是大宗商品里最重要的一点，当下也确实很相关，但同时也有对增长和增长机会的获取。

turns.en: So it's really trying to fit into an investor's portfolio to cover some of those diversification and inflation sensitivity needs, but to do so in a way that we think sort of maximizes those impacts.
turns.zh: 所以它其实是想融入投资者的组合，去覆盖其中一部分分散化和通胀敏感性的需求，而且是用一种我们认为能最大化这些效果的方式去做。

turns.en: When you look at CCNR, it is much more upstream generally than some of the passive indices out there. We're really focused on, within energy, we're focused on upstream oil and gas E&P companies, the companies that are going out drilling wells and extracting oil and gas out of the ground as opposed to purely focusing on large integrated energy companies like direct sands and chevrons of the world.
turns.zh: 当你看 CCNR，它通常比市面上一些被动指数更偏上游。我们真正聚焦的是——在能源板块里，我们聚焦上游的油气勘探与生产（E&P）公司，也就是那些出去钻井、把油气从地里开采出来的公司，而不是纯粹盯着像 Chevron 这类大型一体化能源公司（integrated energy companies）。

turns.en: We generally include that industry, nothing against those companies, but when you look at which industries are more sensitive and better reflect underlying crude or natural gas prices, it's those companies closer to the underlying production, which kind of makes sense.
turns.zh: 我们通常也会纳入那个行业，对那些公司没有任何偏见，但当你看哪些行业更敏感、更能反映底层原油或天然气价格时，是那些更贴近底层生产的公司，这也说得通。

turns.en: And that's what we do across the board. We deal it within the four main sectors we look at, energy, agriculture, base metals and precious metals, and we're really trying to target the industries and companies that are the most upstream and will best deliver the underlying commodity price exposure and all the benefits that come with it.
turns.zh: 这也是我们一贯的做法。我们聚焦于四大主要板块——能源、农业、基本金属（base metals）和贵金属（precious metals），真正想去锁定那些最上游、最能传递底层商品价格敞口以及随之而来所有好处的行业和公司。

turns.en: At the same time, highly diversified, usually over 300 names, roughly 300 names in the portfolio. The idea being, if we spread our risk around enough names, we will better deliver the underlying commodity price exposure to the end investor.
turns.zh: 与此同时，高度分散，通常有 300 多只、大约 300 只标的在组合里。理念是，如果我们把风险分散到足够多的标的上，就能更好地把底层商品价格敞口传递给终端投资者。

turns.en: So a great example of where that was beneficial to us happened last year when a company, Freeport Macmaran, had a mudslide event at their mine in Indonesia, the Graspburg Copper Mine, one of the biggest copper mines in the world, second largest copper mine in the world.
turns.zh: 有个很好的例子能说明这对我们的益处，发生在去年：一家公司 Freeport-McMoRan，在印尼的矿场发生了一起泥石流事件，就是 Grasberg 铜矿，世界上最大的铜矿之一，第二大铜矿。

turns.en: That sent copper prices up 4% that day because copper is a very tight market at the moment, especially with AI data centers, all these uses we have for copper.
turns.zh: 那天铜价上涨了 4%，因为铜目前是一个非常紧张的市场，尤其是有了 AI 数据中心，以及我们对铜的这些用途。

turns.en: But the stock of Freeport dropped like 20% on that day. So if you were just using Freeport as your proxy for copper, you would have been in trouble on that day, but we held, I believe, 12 different copper miners in the portfolio, including Freeport at the time.
turns.zh: 但 Freeport 的股价那天跌了大约 20%。所以如果你只拿 Freeport 当作铜的代理，那天你就会摊上麻烦；但我们当时组合里持有大约 12 家不同的铜矿公司，包括 Freeport。

turns.en: But our basket of those 12 names was up about 4% right along copper prices. I'd use that as an example because that's what we're trying to do across the commodity complex is provide the underlying price exposure by diversifying across enough highly upstream names.
turns.zh: 但我们这 12 只标的组成的篮子当天上涨了约 4%，跟铜价基本同步。我举这个例子，是因为这正是我们想在整个人类大宗商品体系（commodity complex）里做的事——通过分散到足够多的高度上游标的，来提供底层的价格敞口。

turns.en: I want to talk a little bit deeper about that because it was a question I had for you specifically which is, can you talk us through why upstream is better for commodity exposure rather than the refiners and other downstream operations?
turns.zh: 关于这一点我想再深入聊聊，因为这正是我特别想问你的问题：能不能给我们讲讲，为什么对大宗商品敞口而言上游更好，而不是炼油商和其他下游（downstream）业务？

turns.en: Absolutely. It goes back to that being closer to the commodity production, better delivers the underlying exposure to the commodities that are produced, and that is where your benefits stem from.
turns.zh: 当然。这还是要回到——越贴近商品生产，就越能更好地传递对所生产商品的底层敞口，而你的好处正是由此而来。

turns.en: Your diversification, your inflation protection, that's coming from the underlying stuff that those companies make as opposed to just idiosyncratic company, single company risk or equity beta.
turns.zh: 你的分散化、你的通胀保护，来自这些公司生产的底层东西，而不是单纯的特质性单一公司风险（idiosyncratic single-company risk）或股票贝塔（equity beta）。

turns.en: You're really getting the benefits to your portfolio from exposure to the underlying natural resources. In our view, if you own the companies closest to that production, you're going to better deliver that underlying natural resources exposure, and empirically, that has been the way it's played out over time.
turns.zh: 你真正是从对底层自然资源的敞口中为组合获取好处。在我们看来，如果你持有最贴近生产的那些公司，你就能更好地传递那种底层自然资源敞口；而从实证上看，长期以来事实也的确如此。

turns.en: We tend to see higher inflation sensitivities with those more upstream names. Can we talk about the structural case for commodities in general because I think it's pretty underappreciated.
turns.zh: 我们往往会在那些更偏上游的标的上看到更高的通胀敏感性。那我们能聊聊大宗商品总体的结构性逻辑（structural case）吗？因为我觉得这一点相当被低估。

turns.en: Producers used to make up 35% of the S&P in the late 70s, and today it's like 5% while tech is the third of the index. Can you walk us through what that shift means for investors going forward?
turns.zh: 生产商在 70 年代末曾占标普（S&P）的 35%，而如今只有大约 5%，同时科技股占了指数的三分之一。能不能给我们讲讲，这一转变对投资者未来意味着什么？

turns.en: Absolutely. It's a great talking point and one that we've been focusing on quite a bit with investors. These are companies that make real things, the energy, the materials, and the food that powers the world, that we need and need more of year in and year out as populations grow, as standards of living rise, all these things we always use more and more and more of.
turns.zh: 当然。这是个很好的切入点，也是近来我们跟投资者反复聚焦的一点。这些是制造真实东西的公司——驱动世界的能源、材料和食物，是我们需要、而且随着人口增长、生活水平提高，年复一年需要更多的东西，我们总是用得越来越多。

turns.en: In the age of AI now, electricity, power, energy is becoming even more of a huge area and in some ways a bottleneck to a lot of that growth.
turns.zh: 在如今的 AI 时代，电力、能源正成为一个更加巨大的领域，某种程度上还是很多这类增长的瓶颈。

turns.en: That is incredibly important yet as you say, you look at something like the S&P 500, 5% in commodity producers and the bulk of that in just a couple of companies.
turns.zh: 这一点极其重要，可正如你所说，你看标普 500（S&P 500）这样的指数，大宗商品生产商只占 5%，而且其中大部分还集中在那么几家公司身上。

turns.en: We feel that investors are, I think many investors assume they have exposure to these companies that make all this real stuff because they own broad-based equities, but then when you look under the hood, you see that you really don't.
turns.zh: 我们觉得——我想很多投资者以为自己持有这些制造真实东西的公司的敞口，因为他们持有宽基股票；但当你去看内部构成（under the hood），你会发现其实并没有。

turns.en: We think investors have been under-allocated to the space because of the rise of tech in those indices as tech has basically over the last 50 years or so, it's become now over a third of the index.
turns.zh: 我们认为投资者一直低配了这个领域，原因是科技股在这些指数里的崛起——过去大约 50 年，科技股如今已经占到指数的三分之一以上。

turns.en: When you looked back in the late 70s, early 80s, roughly a third of the index as you pointed to was companies that make real stuff. That transition has shifted investor portfolios, maybe without them being fully aware of that.
turns.zh: 而回看 70 年代末、80 年代初，正如你指出的，大约三分之一的指数是那些制造真实东西的公司。这一转变已经悄悄改变了投资者的组合，也许他们自己都没完全意识到。

turns.en: I think as we've highlighted that point with investors, it's really been one that they've taken into account and has resonated with them because they see just how much exposure they have to the Magnificent Seven or whatever we're calling it nowadays and how little they have to these kinds of companies.
turns.zh: 我想，当我们跟投资者强调这一点时，他们真的听进去了、也产生了共鸣，因为他们看到自己对 Magnificent Seven（七巨头）之类的敞口有多大，而对这类公司的敞口有多小。

turns.en: We all understand and I think can see and get the demand side of the equation, but on the supply side, I think I read you pointed out that a new copper mine can take 15 years from planning to production, and investment in new production is really lagged.
turns.zh: 需求端我们都能理解、也看得到、抓得住；但供给端，我记得读到过你指出，一座新的铜矿从规划到投产可能要 15 年，而对新产能的投资严重滞后。

turns.en: How big is that supply gap and where do we see it show up first? I think it's very big and it varies depending on what market you're looking at.
turns.zh: 这个供给缺口有多大？我们会最先在哪里看到它显现？我觉得非常大，而且要看你看的是哪个市场，各不相同。

turns.en: I think copper is a great example of, unlike technology companies, software companies, the production of natural resources is not a light switch.
turns.zh: 我觉得铜就是个很好的例子：跟科技公司、软件公司不同，自然资源的生产不是一个开关（light switch）。

turns.en: Even if we invested the money we should have invested decades ago today, it's going to take a very long time before that capex spend translates through to new production and new supply and companies are reticent to do it these days.
turns.zh: 即便我们今天就把几十年前本该投的钱投下去，也要过很久，这些资本开支（capex）才会转化为新的产能和新的供给；而且如今公司也不愿意这么干。

turns.en: We had energy companies back prior to the pandemic spending, in many cases, these zombie companies that had borrowed so much money and it was so profitable for Wall Street to lend money to that industry.
turns.zh: 疫情之前，能源公司当时在花大钱，很多情况下这些是“僵尸公司”（zombie companies），借了太多的钱，而给这个行业放贷对华尔街来说又太赚钱了。

turns.en: They borrowed so much money and all of a sudden when prices fell during the pandemic, many companies ended up going bankrupt or really in financial straits.
turns.zh: 他们借了太多钱，结果疫情期间价格一跌，很多公司最终破产，或者陷入真正的财务困境。

turns.en: They've come around to a new mentality, which is capital restraint, focusing on improving margins, returning cash flows to investors, and that's something we've seen in the mining space as well.
turns.zh: 他们转而接受了一种新的心态，那就是资本克制（capital restraint）：专注于改善利润率、把现金流返还给投资者，这一点我们在矿业领域也看到了。

turns.en: The problem is these companies are very comfortable, I think, in the position they are today, financially very strong, shareholders are happy, they're paying down debt, they're buying back shares, they're returning dividends to their shareholders.
turns.zh: 问题是，这些公司对目前的处境我觉得是很舒服的——财务上非常稳健，股东很满意，他们在还债、回购股票、给股东派息。

turns.en: There's not really an appetite for capex spend and we haven't seen it and if prices go higher because we're not increasing the supply to match the demand, the companies continue to benefit.
turns.zh: 他们并没有真正增加资本开支的意愿，我们也没看到；而如果价格上涨，是因为我们没有增加供给去匹配需求，那这些公司还是会持续受益。

turns.en: I think that gap is pretty wide, particularly in something like copper and we don't really see many signs of it closing. We don't see a lot of investment in new greenfield supply.
turns.zh: 我觉得这个缺口相当大，尤其是在铜这类品种上，而且我们基本看不到它在收窄的迹象。我们看不到对新绿地（greenfield）供给的太多投资。

turns.en: We sort of see incremental marginal technological improvements, enhancing productivity, brownfield expansion, expanding existing mines, but we're not seeing a lot of greenfield development and I think that's what we really need.
turns.zh: 我们看到的更多是渐进的、边际的技术改进，提升生产率，以及棕地扩张（brownfield expansion），也就是扩展现有的矿；但我们没看到太多绿地开发（greenfield development），而这我觉得才是我们真正需要的。

turns.en: It's sort of no secret that the copper market is extremely tight and it's heading for a bigger imbalance in supply and demand by the end of the decade, yet we're not really seeing any action happening to try to remedy that.
turns.zh: 铜市场极度紧张、并且到本十年末会走向更大的供需失衡，这几乎已不是秘密；可我们却基本没看到任何试图去缓解这一情况的行动。

turns.en: Supply and demand in commodities generally means that the prices are going to have to go up to compensate for that imbalance. Can we stay on copper and the AI data center trade here just for a minute just because it's so popular?
turns.zh: 大宗商品里的供需通常意味着，价格将不得不涨上去，以补偿这种失衡。那我们能在这儿在铜和 AI 数据中心这个交易主题上再停留一会儿吗？就因为它太火了。

turns.en: We definitely have talked about copper, but other things like natural gas, uranium is even being talked about again. How is CCNR positioned to take advantage of some of these different areas in commodity exposure?
turns.zh: 我们确实谈了不少铜，但还有别的东西，比如天然气，甚至铀（uranium）又被人谈论起来了。CCNR 是如何布局，去抓住大宗商品敞口里这些不同领域的？

turns.en: Yeah, it's one of the things I think that does set it apart from many of the passive indices and competitors out there. Because we built this thing from the ground up and we built it in a way that we thought made the most sense, we do include a lot of exposure to a lot of things you won't see.
turns.zh: 是的，我觉得这正是让它区别于市面上很多被动指数和竞品的地方之一。因为我们是自下而上、从零把这个东西搭起来的，而且是用我们认为最合理的方式搭的，所以我们确实纳入了很多你在别处看不到的敞口。

turns.en: And other indices. Uranium is a great example. There's not a ton of uranium companies out there that one can own in a sufficiently liquid fashion.
turns.zh: 在别的指数里就没有。铀是个很好的例子。市面上能以足够流动性的方式持有的铀公司并不多。

turns.en: But there are some and we generally include uranium as an industry in our portfolios. Natural gas, you can certainly, plenty of producers out there, but that's going to be a huge area going forward.
turns.zh: 但还是有一些，我们通常会把铀作为一个行业纳入组合。天然气当然也可以，市面上有很多生产商，而且未来这会是一个巨大的领域。

turns.en: But so is some of the renewable and alternative energy, which are things that we have included in our energy portfolio. When you look at the fact that roughly 20% of US power production is coming from renewable and alternative sources, that should be in an energy portfolio in our mind.
turns.zh: 但可再生能源和替代能源也是如此，这些我们已经纳入了能源组合。当你看到美国大约 20% 的电力生产来自可再生和替代能源，在我们看来，这就应该被放进一个能源组合里。

turns.en: Even if passive indices, market cap weighted indices, these more legacy approaches don't include those. So because we're actively managed, because we construct the portfolio the way we do, we have tried to include those sorts of things that are more relevant to your point.
turns.zh: 即便被动指数、市值加权指数这些更传统的做法并不纳入它们。所以，正因为我们是主动管理的、正因为我们是这样构建组合的，我们才试着去纳入那些更贴合你所说观点的东西。

turns.en: AI data centers are a great point. We're going to need energy, kind of, I like to say all of the above. It's not just going to be the natural gas, although that is going to be a huge component of it.
turns.zh: AI 数据中心是个很好的点。我们将需要能源，我喜欢说“以上全部都要”（all of the above）。不会只是天然气，尽管天然气会是其中很大的一块。

turns.en: It's also going to be these renewable and alternative sources. It's going to be uranium. We're going to need so much more energy. We're not going to get to be that picky about where we get it from.
turns.zh: 还会是这些可再生和替代能源，还会是铀。我们将需要多得多的能源，我们没条件去挑剔它从哪儿来。

turns.en: And I think that's one of the advantages our product provides, is that it does have that really broad based exposure. So you don't have to try to predict, is it just going to be natural gas or solar or wind?
turns.zh: 我觉得这正是我们产品提供的优势之一——它确实有那种非常宽泛的敞口。所以你不必去预测，到底是天然气，还是太阳能、风能。

turns.en: You kind of own it all. And I'm very confident that we're going to need more and more energy going forward from all those different sources.
turns.zh: 你差不多把它们全持有了。而我非常有信心，未来我们会需要来自所有这些不同来源的、越来越多的能源。

turns.en: And I think it's one of the ways we're differentiated. In metals, similarly, we include things like lithium specialty metals, these things that are becoming more and more relevant.
turns.zh: 我觉得这也是我们差异化的方式之一。在金属方面也是类似的，我们纳入了像锂、特种金属（specialty metals）这些东西，这些正变得越来越有相关性。

turns.en: It's always been in the DNA of the product to try to include as many globally important relevant commodities as possible. Just looking through the portfolio, I know you guys aren't allowed to really talk about individual names, but you've got agriculture-linked names and timber producers in here.
turns.zh: 尽可能多地纳入全球重要、有相关性的大宗商品，一直都写在这只产品的基因（DNA）里。就翻看一下组合，我知道你们其实不太被允许谈个股（individual names），但你们这里有农业相关的标的，还有木材生产商。

turns.en: Why does things like agriculture and timber belong in a conversation in a commodity spun like this? Absolutely. So agriculture is obviously incredibly important.
turns.zh: 为什么像农业和木材这样的东西，会属于这样一个大宗商品基金里的讨论范畴？当然。农业显然极其重要。

turns.en: It's all the food and everything that we need and use every day. And it is one of the areas where it is more interesting, I think, on the equity side, because it's not quite as direct a link as, say, on the energy side.
turns.zh: 它是我们每天需要和使用的所有食物和一切。而且在股票这一侧，我觉得它是更有意思的领域之一，因为它不像能源那一侧那样有那么直接的关联。

turns.en: So you can't go out and buy publicly traded farming companies or corn companies or wheat companies like we see on the future side of things.
turns.zh: 所以你没法像我们在期货那一侧看到的那样，出去买公开上市的农场公司、玉米公司或小麦公司。

turns.en: But what we can own are things like fertilizers, things like water companies, things like seed producers and herbicide and pesticide companies, all those inputs into the growing and production of food, including things like agricultural machinery tends to be one of the highly correlated areas to the underlying agriculture prices because you need John Deere tract or what have you to harvest all that food.
turns.zh: 但我们能持有的，是像化肥、水务公司、种子生产商，以及除草剂和杀虫剂公司这些东西——所有那些投入到食物种植和生产里的东西，包括农业机械，往往是与底层农业价格高度相关的领域之一，因为你需要 John Deere 拖拉机之类的来收割所有这些食物。

turns.en: So sort of the inputs and the tools for the outputs is how we get it on the agriculture side. And again, it's energy, stuff, and food. That's kind of the three main things in natural resources, and that's how we get our exposure on the ag side.
turns.zh: 所以在农业这一侧，我们是通过投入品和用于产出的工具来获取敞口的。再说一遍，就是能源、材料（stuff）和食物，这差不多是自然资源里的三大主线，这也是我们在农业侧获取敞口的方式。

turns.en: So you've got some real international exposure, too, in the fund. How important is the global scope versus a U.S.-only natural resources fund?
turns.zh: 所以这只基金里也有不少真正的国际化敞口。相较于一只只投美国的自然资源基金，全球范围有多重要？

turns.en: It's incredibly important. Commodities are global, natural resources are global, they're produced all over the world, they're consumed all over the world.
turns.zh: 极其重要。大宗商品是全球性的，自然资源是全球性的，它们在世界各地生产，也在世界各地消费。

turns.en: Certain geographies have certain natural resources and others don't. When we look at things like platinum and PGM metals, a lot of that is coming from places like South Africa.
turns.zh: 某些地区拥有某些自然资源，而另一些则没有。当我们看像铂和铂族金属（PGM metals）这类东西时，很多都来自南非这样的地方。

turns.en: It's just what that country was blessed with in terms of its natural resources. Here in the U.S., we have abundant crude oil, natural gas, and these hydrocarbon products.
turns.zh: 这就是那个国家在自然资源方面被赋予的禀赋。而在美国，我们拥有丰富的原油、天然气和这些碳氢化合物（hydrocarbon）产品。

turns.en: But those get used all over the world, right? So the portfolio is really meant to reflect that. We tend to be, on average, I think about 40% U.S., with 60% being international.
turns.zh: 但这些在世界各地都被使用，对吧？所以这个组合真的是想反映这一点。我们平均下来，我觉得大约 40% 是美国，60% 是国际。

turns.en: And that's really more a function of what companies are available to us to invest in, on which exchanges, can we access them? And then we put everything together in the portfolio and that's kind of where it shakes out.
turns.zh: 而这更多取决于有哪些公司可供我们投资、在哪些交易所、我们能不能接触到它们；然后我们把一切拼进组合里，大致就是这么个结果。

turns.en: But also important, I think, in that is the fact that there's a correlation, an inverse correlation between broad commodity prices and the dollar.
turns.zh: 但我觉得同样重要的是，大宗商品整体价格与美元之间存在一种相关性——一种负相关（inverse correlation）。

turns.en: When the dollar goes up, commodity prices tend to go down vice versa because it's purchasing power of a dollar. So by having a portion of our portfolio outside the U.S., we're sort of enhancing that commodity-like nature of the product because we're not hedging that foreign currency exposure back to dollars.
turns.zh: 当美元上涨，商品价格往往下跌，反之亦然，因为这关乎美元的购买力。所以，通过把组合的一部分放在美国以外，我们某种程度上是在增强这个产品的“类商品”属性，因为我们不会把那部分外币敞口对冲回美元。

turns.en: We're keeping it in the local currency. That adds an additional layer of enhancement of that commodity-like diversification you're getting. Now, if you were in something that was more North America-focused, there is an index out there.
turns.zh: 我们把它保留在当地货币里。这就为你获得的这种“类商品”分散化，又叠加了一层增强。那么，如果你投的是更聚焦北美的那种，市面上是有一个指数的。

turns.en: I won't pick on them, but they are more North American-focused natural resources. You would see a lot more energy because that's what we have here in North America.
turns.zh: 我不想去点名挑刺，但它们是更聚焦北美的自然资源。你会看到多得多的能源，因为这就是我们在北美所拥有的。

turns.en: We have nothing against energy. It's our largest sector as well, but we don't think it should be 80% of the portfolio. We think it should be around about 40%.
turns.zh: 我们对能源没有任何偏见，它也是我们最大的板块，但我们不觉得它应该占组合的 80%，我们认为它应该在 40% 左右。

turns.en: So by diversifying globally, we're really getting at just that broader swath of natural resources exposure. So just out of curiosity on the active side, is there a point in your process where it sounds like to me you're trying to get as correlated as exposure as you can using actual companies to get this commodity exposure instead of just going out and buying futures?
turns.zh: 所以通过全球分散，我们真正获取的是那更宽广的一片自然资源敞口。那么出于好奇，在主动管理这一侧——听上去你们是在尽量用真实公司去获得尽可能相关的敞口，来得到这种商品敞口，而不是直接出去买期货。

turns.en: Is there any part of your process that you're looking at the fundamentals of a company and saying, hey, we don't want to own this company even though it gives us the exposure?
turns.zh: 你们的流程里，有没有哪一部分是在看一家公司的基本面，然后说“嘿，即便它能给我们敞口，我们也不想持有这家公司”？

turns.en: Absolutely. So the way we actually do our active management, because as you point out as an actively managed fund, is we leverage a systematic data-driven quantitative process to do our portfolio construction.
turns.zh: 当然。我们做主动管理的方式——正如你指出的，它是一只主动管理型基金——是我们借助一套系统化的、数据驱动的量化流程（quantitative process）来做组合构建。

turns.en: But it's all very much rooted in common sense fundamentals. The term that used to get used was quantum mental. It's fallen out of favor, but that's the style of it.
turns.zh: 但这一切都深深扎根于常识性的基本面。过去常用的一个词是 quantamental（量化基本面），现在已经不太流行了，但风格就是那样。

turns.en: So it's leveraging our expertise in commodities and our background as really fundamentals commodities people, along with my background that's more quantitative, technical, systematic.
turns.zh: 所以它是把我们在大宗商品上的专长、我们作为真正的基本面大宗商品人的背景，与我更偏量化、技术、系统化的背景结合起来。

turns.en: And what we're doing is we're using a number of different what we call portfolio drivers or models. Each one is looking at a single factor. And some might be operating at a sector level to overweight or underweight sectors.
turns.zh: 我们做的，是使用一系列我们称为“组合驱动因子”（portfolio drivers）或模型的东西。每一个都在看单一的一个因子。有些可能在板块层面运作，去超配或低配某些板块。

turns.en: Some might be operating at an individual company level or an industry level within sectors. So a couple examples that might make it a little more clear.
turns.zh: 有些可能在单个公司层面、或板块内的行业层面运作。举几个例子也许能讲得更清楚一些。

turns.en: We'll look at things like the term structure in the futures markets on a sector level. That's the futures term structure that's telling you something about supply and demand in those futures markets.
turns.zh: 我们会在板块层面去看期货市场的期限结构（term structure）。正是这个期货期限结构，在告诉你那些期货市场里供需的某些信息。

turns.en: We'll translate that over and say, OK, all else being equal, if something like the energy sector is showing a lot of what we call backwardation or a tight market where supply and demand are mismatched in the favor of demand, outstripping, supply, all else being equal, we'd want to own more energy companies in our portfolio and less of the other sectors.
turns.zh: 我们会把它转译过来，然后说：好，在其他条件相同的情况下，如果像能源板块正表现出大量我们所说的 backwardation（期货贴水），也就是一个供需错配、需求超过供给的紧张市场——那么在其他条件相同时，我们会想在组合里持有更多能源公司、更少其他板块。

turns.en: But then we might look within energy companies and look within, let's say, E&P companies and look at the extraction margins of each company and say, all else being equal, we'd prefer to own companies that can extract oil and gas out of the ground more cheaply than their competitors.
turns.zh: 然后我们可能会在能源公司内部再看，比如在 E&P 公司里，去看每一家公司的开采利润率（extraction margins），然后说：在其他条件相同时，我们更想持有那些能比竞争对手更便宜地把油气从地里开采出来的公司。

turns.en: And so we'll say we want to have more exposure to those single names that are getting better margins and less exposure to the names with worse margins.
turns.zh: 所以我们会说，我们想对这些利润率更好的个股有更多敞口，对利润率更差的标的有更少敞口。

turns.en: And we do that across a number of different factors, roughly 25 or so. We're always looking to improve those, add new ones, take ones away when they no longer are adding alpha to the process.
turns.zh: 我们会在一系列不同的因子上这么做，大约 25 个左右。我们始终在改进它们、加入新的、并在某些因子不再为流程贡献 alpha 时把它们去掉。

turns.en: But that's sort of the active management process. The collection of, we think, sort of unique factors that we're looking at leveraging our expertise in commodities markets just applied systematically because when you have to practically manage a portfolio of 300 or more names, it kind of lends itself to that type of approach.
turns.zh: 但这大致就是主动管理的流程——一组我们认为相当独特的因子的集合，借助我们在大宗商品市场上的专长，只是系统化地去运用；因为当你必须在实践中管理一个 300 只甚至更多标的的组合时，它就自然而然适合这种方法。

turns.en: So with CCNR, it carries a lower beta than broader equities and a lower correlation to the S&P. So I'm an advisor listening to this, and I've got a diversified model portfolio.
turns.zh: 所以 CCNR 的贝塔（beta）比宽基股票更低，与标普的相关性也更低。那么假设我是一名正在听这期节目的投顾，我有一个分散化的模型组合（model portfolio）。

turns.en: Like, two-parter, what's the case for having commodities exposure period? And how would you use this fund in a diversified model portfolio? Absolutely.
turns.zh: 这是个两问的问题：持有大宗商品敞口这件事本身，理由是什么？以及你会怎么在一个分散化的模型组合里使用这只基金？当然。

turns.en: So the case for commodities exposure, right now, let's split that into the tactical case versus the strategic case. We do think there is value in having a strategic allocation, mainly, again, for that diversified diversification and inflation sensitivity.
turns.zh: 关于大宗商品敞口的理由，眼下我们把它拆成战术性（tactical）的和战略性（strategic）的两方面。我们确实认为持有一个战略性配置是有价值的，主要还是要归功于那种分散化和通胀敏感性。

turns.en: When you look at the things that are typically used for inflation sensitivity in a portfolio, you're thinking commodities and natural resources, EM exposure, tips, those sorts of things, the sensitivity to inflation is highest amongst commodities and natural resources by a wide margin.
turns.zh: 当你看组合里通常用来做通胀敏感性的那些东西——你会想到大宗商品和自然资源、新兴市场（EM）敞口、TIPS（通胀保值债券）之类——对通胀的敏感性在大宗商品和自然资源中是最高的，而且高出一大截。

turns.en: That's important because if you have something that has a beta to inflation of five or six, that means every dollar you put in your portfolio into that thing is going to cover an additional four or five dollars of exposure elsewhere, right?
turns.zh: 这一点很重要，因为如果某个东西对通胀的贝塔是五或六，那就意味着你每往组合里放一美元到那个东西上，就能额外覆盖别处四到五美元的敞口，对吧？

turns.en: And that's the idea, is you want to put the most inflation sensitive thing in because you're not going to own 100% of your portfolio in these things, you're trying to get the most bang for your buck through that high inflation sensitivity.
turns.zh: 所以理念就是，你想把最通胀敏感的东西放进去，因为你不会把组合的 100% 都押在这些东西上，你是想通过那种高通胀敏感性，把钱花得最值（most bang for your buck）。

turns.en: So that's where we see it being used. Some advisors and end users have real assets buckets. It fits nicely as a part of a real assets bucket.
turns.zh: 这就是我们看到它被使用的地方。一些投顾和终端用户有“实物资产”（real assets）的桶，它能很好地作为实物资产桶的一部分。

turns.en: But also, in the case of CCNR, I think it's important to keep in mind, they're not commodity futures, strictly speaking, they're equities. And we think that they have a place sort of in your overall equity allocation as opposed to just a small sliver of a sliver of a real assets allocation.
turns.zh: 但同样，就 CCNR 而言，我觉得要记住的一点很重要：严格来说它们不是商品期货，而是股票。我们认为它们在你整体的股票配置里有一席之地，而不只是实物资产配置里那一小块中的一小块。

turns.en: Obviously, you take that with a grain of salt coming from me, but that is where we do see a good fit, like we talked about earlier, just trying to diversify that really tech-heavy broad equity you have because, again, the strategic case is diversification inflation protection.
turns.zh: 当然，这话从我嘴里说出来，你听听就好（take that with a grain of salt）；但这确实是我们看到的一个很好的契合点，就像我们前面聊的，就是去分散你那个科技含量非常高的宽基股票，因为再说一次，战略性理由就是分散化和通胀保护。

turns.en: The tactical case I think is really interesting these days is potentially a way to gain exposure to what's happening with infrastructure, AI, nearshoring and on-shoring trends, military spending and rearmament.
turns.zh: 而战术性理由我觉得当下很有意思，它可能是一种获取敞口的方式，去把握基础设施、AI、近岸外包（nearshoring）与回岸（on-shoring）趋势、军费开支与再武装（rearmament）正在发生的事。

turns.en: There's a lot of tailwinds to this asset class right now. But we haven't really seen the investment dollars flow into it. And like we talked about earlier, we haven't seen the CAPEX on the company side being spent like we've seen the CAPEX of the hyperscalers and things.
turns.zh: 眼下这个资产类别有很多顺风（tailwinds）。但我们其实还没看到投资资金流进来；就像我们前面聊的，我们也没看到公司侧的资本开支（CAPEX）像那些超大规模云厂商（hyperscalers）之类的资本开支那样被花出去。

turns.en: So these companies haven't ramped up spending in reaction to things like AI. But they do stand to benefit greatly if all this infrastructure ends up getting built.
turns.zh: 所以这些公司并没有因为 AI 之类的事情而加大开支。但如果所有这些基础设施最终真的建起来，它们确实会大大受益。

turns.en: So from a tactical standpoint, we think it's a really interesting time and we see the risk and reward really being skewed less to the downside, I would say, because you haven't seen these companies doubling down on all this spending.
turns.zh: 所以从战术角度看，我们认为这是一个非常有意思的时点，而且我们看到风险回报（risk and reward）其实更偏向不那么大的下行，我会这么说，因为你还没看到这些公司在所有这些开支上加倍下注。

turns.en: They've sort of just been sitting, enjoying good margins and we think investors are starting to take notice. Well, Doug, I really appreciate you being here with me today.
turns.zh: 它们某种程度上就一直待在那儿，享受着不错的利润率，而我们认为投资者正开始注意到这一点。嗯，Doug，我真的很感谢你今天能来我这儿。

turns.en: But before I let you go, where can people learn more about core commodity and your CCNR ETF? Absolutely. More about the ETF, you can definitely find on our partners, the Alps Funds website and the CCNR page there.
turns.zh: 但在放你走之前，大家可以在哪里更多地了解 Core Commodity 和你们的 CCNR ETF？当然。关于这只 ETF，你肯定可以在我们的合作伙伴 Alps Funds 网站、以及那里的 CCNR 页面上找到。

turns.en: We also have a website, corecommodityllc.com, that people can go to and take a look as well. Well, again, thanks for being with me today, Doug.
turns.zh: 我们还有一个网站 corecommodityllc.com，大家也可以去看看。嗯，再次感谢你今天来，Doug。

turns.en: I really appreciate it, Brad. Thank you for having me.
turns.zh: 我非常感激，Brad。谢谢你邀请我。
